statement: [src] limine-entry-tool reads its settings in four layers, lowest priority first: `/usr/share/limine-entry-tool.d/`, `/etc/limine-entry-tool.conf`, `/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/`, then `/etc/default/limine` (highest).
host_value: [obs] `/etc/limine-entry-tool.conf:84` `ENABLE_VERIFICATION=yes` (byte-identical to the 1.40.0 package file, sha256 `44207b64…`); `/etc/default/limine` sets no `ENABLE_VERIFICATION`; `/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/` holds only `resume.conf`; `/usr/share/limine-entry-tool.d/` absent

statement: [src] Pins are written only when `ENABLE_VERIFICATION` is `yes` (case-insensitive) AND the `b2sum` command exists; otherwise the tool writes the path with no `#` at all. The default is off.
[src] The pin is appended to the `path:` line of a UKI entry and to every `module_path:` and the `path:` of a kernel+initramfs entry; `cmdline:` and `comment:` lines never get one.
host_value: [obs] both main entries are UKIs; only their `path:` lines carry pins (lines 30, 38)

statement: [src] The hash is the `b2sum` command's output (BLAKE2b-512, matching Limine's 128-hex rule), computed twice in parallel; on disagreement it retries, and after the last retry it logs "Hardware is faulty" and still returns the first result.

[src] The packaged repair command is `limine-update`: it runs `limine-install --no-efi-register` and then `limine-mkinitcpio` with the caller's arguments, which is the path that re-adds entries and so rewrites their pins from the files as they are then. limine-entry-tool 1.40.0 has no hash-only refresh option (its `Main.java` options are add/remove/scan/tree/cmdline).

[src] limine-snapper-sync builds a snapshot entry from the main entry's `path:` line: it cuts the first `#hex` run off that line and appends that same text to the history-file path it writes. It never recomputes the BLAKE2b.
host_value: [obs] existing history pins (lines 50, 56, 64) date from 2026-10-20, before the incident; r87 read them OK

statement: [src] The history file is named after the current file's content hash (`HASH_FUNCTION`, default SHA-256), computed fresh at sync time. Its integrity check compares that name suffix with the content, never the `#` pin.

[inf] Consequence on this host: until the main pins are recomputed (PW5), every snapshot entry limine-snapper-sync adds for `linux` or `linux-lts` carries the stale main pin (`b990d8c6…`/`a68c281d…`, PW6) next to a history copy of the rewritten UKI (`57f5eb94…`/`eff78d32…`, PW7), so it reads `LP-MISMATCH` (`prompt` under `hash_mismatch_panic: no`). The stale pin spreads with each new snapshot; the hourly "Updated" runs leave the main pins as they are. Not executed: no snapshot was created this round.
